facts.text: A stereo camera uses two cameras a known distance apart to estimate distance, while a depth camera (RGB-D) provides a color image and a distance for every pixel.
facts.quote: A stereo camera uses two cameras a known distance apart to work out how far away things are, and a depth camera (RGB-D) delivers a color image plus a distance for every pixel.

facts.text: A wider stereo-camera baseline improves accuracy at long range.
facts.quote: A wider baseline gives better accuracy at long range.

facts.text: Stereo and depth cameras have general camera weaknesses; stereo matching also struggles with textureless surfaces, and active depth-camera types have short range.
facts.quote: Weaknesses are those of cameras in general, plus textureless surfaces with nothing to match, and short range for active types.

facts.text: A fielded forklift system uses a rear stereo camera to distinguish people from objects and slows the forklift by cutting power rather than braking.
facts.quote: a forklift system whose rear stereo camera tells people from objects and slows by cutting power rather than braking

facts.text: A fielded utility-loader system combines cameras, a stereo camera and radar.
facts.quote: a utility-loader system combining cameras, a stereo camera and radar [Chapter 2]

facts.text: Simulation of time-of-flight depth cameras needs multipath models and sensor-specific depth-noise models.
facts.quote: Time-of-flight depth cameras need multipath and sensor-specific depth-noise models in simulation [Chapter 6].

facts.text: Camera depth is cheap and provides perception with a distance per object.
facts.quote: Camera depth is cheap and gives perception a distance per object

facts.text: No validation of camera-depth sensors for heavy-machine braking in dust or darkness was found.
facts.quote: no validation of such sensors for heavy-machine braking in dust or darkness was found [Chapter 6].
